accept: left ventricular thrombus after anterior infarction

findings: Q waves of a previous anterior infarction
Persistent ST elevation in the aneurysm territory

echoTasks.find: Echogenic mass in the apex distinct from trabeculation with absent independent motion
Protruding mobile clot with a broad base over an akinetic apex and anterior wall
Apical aneurysm with contrast opacifying around the mass on a contrast study

auscultation.added: Third sound as the ventricle is dilated
auscultation.murmur: Soft pansystolic murmur of functional regurgitation

exam.general: Older man, comfortable at rest, mild breathlessness on exertion, no focal deficit
exam.other: No carotid bruit, no oedema, lungs clear

history.a: Anterior MI three weeks ago treated with thrombolysis at the district hospital, now stable
No weakness, no speech change, no visual loss since discharge
Continues dual antiplatelets and statin, admits missing doses twice
Diabetic for 10 years, hypertensive for 6 years
Retired teacher, walks daily, anxious about another attack
No bleeding history, no ulcer, no alcohol

keyPoints: Start warfarin with an INR target of 2 to 3 alongside antiplatelets for the shortest needed overlap, per the AHA STEMI guidance on left ventricular thrombus
Arrange serial echo at 3 months to confirm resolution before stopping anticoagulation
Counsel on bleed signs, NSAID avoidance, and diet steadiness for warfarin control
Optimise secondary prevention with statin, beta blocker and ACE inhibitor alongside antiplatelets
Screen for embolic events at each visit with a focused neuro and limb check
management.model: Warfarin to INR 2 to 3 with limited antiplatelet overlap, serial imaging to resolution, and bleed counselling

accept: Q waves with persistent ST elevation
required.answer: anterior Q waves with persistent ST elevation

sources: AHA guideline on ST elevation myocardial infarction with left ventricular thrombus advice, in own words
ASE chamber quantification guideline, in own words
stem: A 60 year old retired teacher from Coimbatore, three weeks after an anterior infarction treated with thrombolysis, attends routine follow up. He has no embolic symptoms and the ECG shows anterior Q waves with persistent ST elevation.
teaching: A mass distinct from trabeculation over an akinetic apex after anterior MI is thrombus until proved otherwise
Large means pedunculated and mobile with high embolic risk, and it needs anticoagulation
Warfarin to INR 2 to 3 with limited overlap is the standard after anterior infarction thrombus
Resolution must be proved on serial imaging before stopping therapy
title: Large left ventricular thrombus after anterior infarction
